title: Course on two-dimensional quantum gases
abstract: This course on two-dimensional quantum gases, prepared for the S{ã}o Paulo ICTP-SAIFR IVth School on Light and Cold Atoms, is organized into three lectures. The first introductory lecture addresses Bose-Einstein condensation in an ideal gas, the effect of interactions in the weakly interacting limit, Gross-Pitaevskii equation and its hydrodynamic formulation, as well as superfluidity. The second lecture is devoted to the main features of two-dimensional quantum gases: importance of the interactions, enhanced phase fluctuations and the emergence of a quasi long-range order, superfluidity through the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless mechanism, scaling symmetry. The third lecture has taken the form of a seminar on fast rotating quasi two-dimensional Bose gases and thermal melting of the vortex lattice. The slides accompanying these notes can be found on the school website: https://www.ictp-saifr.org/slca2025/.
summary: This course material provides a detailed theoretical review of quantum gases, covering the transition to BEC in trapped systems using the Gross-Pitaevskii equation. It emphasizes the unique physics of two-dimensional gases, deriving the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless mechanism and analyzing the resulting quasi long-range order through correlation functions.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental physics of Bose-Einstein Condensation (BEC) and superfluidity in quantum gases, with a specific focus on the unique behavior observed in two-dimensional (2D) systems.
main_result: It establishes quantitative criteria for BEC based on the density of states and derives the governing Gross-Pitaevskii Equation (GPE) for the condensate wavefunction. Furthermore, it details the quasi long-range order characteristic of 2D superfluids via the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) mechanism.
method: The analysis employs a combination of mean-field theory (GPE derivation), semi-classical approximations for thermodynamic quantities, and linear response theory/Bogoliubov approach for analyzing phase fluctuations.
model_or_system: The primary system is a weakly interacting Bose gas, modeled in various dimensionalities (3D, 2D, quasi-2D) confined by isotropic power-law traps. The interactions are modeled via an effective contact potential, leading to the GPE.
key_observables: Condensate fraction ($N_0/N$), first-order correlation function ($G_1(r)$), critical temperature ($T_c$), and the superfluid order parameter.
important_parameters: Dimensionality ($D$), trap exponent ($\alpha$), interaction strength ($g$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the semi-classical limit for thermodynamics and the assumption that density fluctuations are negligible when analyzing phase correlations in 2D.
figures_summary: The notes reference figures showing the BEC fraction dependence on temperature for different trap geometries and the decay of the correlation function $G_1(r)$ in 2D systems.
paper_structure: The content is structured logically, moving from the general theory of BEC in trapped gases (ideal gas, interactions, GPE) to the specific, advanced topic of 2D systems, culminating in the analysis of phase fluctuations and the BKT transition.
why_interesting: This work provides a comprehensive theoretical treatment of dimensionality effects on superfluidity, which is a cornerstone topic in modern AMO physics, bridging mean-field descriptions with fluctuation-dominated regimes.

Figure 1.5: Demonstration of a critical velocity in a 2D gas. Left: A focused laser is stirred around the gas, at some fixed distance from the center, and at a fixed linear speed v. Right: The energy transferred to the gas is measured in a time-of-flight experiment. At low v, no energy is transferred. Above a critical value vc, the energy increases quadratically with v −vc, due to the creation of excited particle out of the BEC. Figure from Ref. [15].

The circulation is an integer number of h/M, qh/M in this latter case. Right: Typical velocity field around a vortex.
